(a) In General.—
        (1) Each of the following provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “March 31, 2012” and inserting “June 30, 2012”:
            (A) Section 4041(a)(1)(C)(iii)(I). 
            (B) Section 4041(m)(1)(B). 
            (C) Section 4081(d)(1).  
        (2) Each of the following provisions of such Code is amended by striking “April 1, 2012” and inserting “July 1, 2012”:
            (A) Section 4041(m)(1)(A). 
            (B) Section 4051(c). 
            (C) Section 4071(d). 
            (D) Section 4081(d)(3).   
    (b) Extension of Tax, etc., on Use of Certain Heavy Vehicles.—Each of the following provisions of such Code is amended by striking “2012” and inserting “2013”:
        (1) Section 4481(f). 
        (2) Subsections (c)(4) and (d) of section 4482.  
    (c) Floor Stocks Refunds.—Section 6412(a)(1) of such Code is amended—
        (1) by striking “April 1, 2012” each place it appears and inserting “July 1, 2012”; 
        (2) by striking “September 30, 2012” each place it appears and inserting “December 31, 2012”; and 
        (3) by striking “July 1, 2012” and inserting “October 1, 2012”.  
    (d) Extension of Certain Exemptions.—Sections 4221(a) and 4483(i) of such Code are each amended by striking “April 1, 2012” and inserting “July 1, 2012”. 
    (e) Extension of Transfers of Certain Taxes.—
        (1) In general.—Section 9503 of such Code is amended—
            (A) in subsection (b)—
                (i) by striking “April 1, 2012” each place it appears in paragraphs (1) and (2) and inserting “July 1, 2012”; 
                (ii) by striking “April 1, 2012” in the heading of paragraph (2) and inserting “July 1, 2012”; 
                (iii) by striking “March 31, 2012” in paragraph (2) and inserting “June 30, 2012”; and 
                (iv) by striking “January 1, 2013” in paragraph (2) and inserting “April 1, 2013”; and  
            (B) in subsection (c)(2), by striking “January 1, 2013” and inserting “April 1, 2013”.  
        (2) Motorboat and small-engine fuel tax transfers.—
            (A) In general.—Paragraphs (3)(A)(i) and (4)(A) of section 9503(c) of such Code are each amended by striking “April 1, 2012” and inserting “July 1, 2012”. 
            (B) Conforming amendments to land and water conservation fund.—Section 201(b) of the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 (16 U.S.C. 460l–11(b)) is amended—
                (i) by striking “April 1, 2013” each place it appears and inserting “July 1, 2013”; and 
                (ii) by striking “April 1, 2012” and inserting “July 1, 2012”.    
    (f) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall take effect on April 1, 2012.

fable.w: This section only extends expiration dates for highway-related excise taxes, exemptions, floor stocks refunds, and trust fund transfers by striking and replacing dates in the Internal Revenue Code. Nothing tempts a Yes reading: there is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. It is purely a technical amendment to tax provisions.
fable.s: Each of the following provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “March 31, 2012” and inserting “June 30, 2012”

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Internal Revenue Code, specifically changing dates for tax provisions and exemptions. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. The changes are legislative directives rather than participatory processes.
qwen_block.s: Each of the following provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “March 31, 2012” and inserting “June 30, 2012”
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section amends tax codes which affect the public, it implicitly involves public participation. However, the text itself only describes technical amendments to dates and sections of the Internal Revenue Code. There is no mechanism described for the public, states, or other outside entities to consult, comment, or participate in the decision to extend these dates. The decision is made by Congress through the statute itself.

opus.w: This section only changes dates in the Internal Revenue Code and the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act to extend certain fuel taxes, heavy-vehicle use taxes, exemptions, floor stocks refunds and trust fund transfers. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The mention of 'refunds' is not participation: a refund claim is like applying for a benefit, and here only the deadlines change.
opus.b: Step 1: The section mentions "Floor Stocks Refunds," which might look like outsiders dealing with the government. It isn't participation. A refund claim is like applying for a benefit, and this text only changes dates anyway. No one outside the federal government is consulted on any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Internal Revenue Code, specifically changing effective dates for various tax provisions. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before these changes are enacted. The changes are legislative mandates, not decisions made through a participatory process.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing tax dates affects the public, so it involves participation. However, the definition requires a specific mechanism of consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties *before* a decision is made. This section merely amends statutory dates; it does not establish a process for public comment, advisory boards, or consultation with states or tribes.
